To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Astn2 is required to generate a parallel hair array on the back of mice.
we identified a genetic modifier of the Frizzled6 (Fz6) -/- hair orientation phenotype and that Astn2 modulates the global orientation of hair follicles in mice.
Astn2 acts as a genetic modifier of Fz6 -/ hair patterning, and this effect results in an inversion of the global hair orientation in the back of Fz6-/-;Astn2ex5del/delmice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the global orientation of hair follicles is established during postnatal development.
understanding the molecular mechanisms that regulate hair patterning.
understanding the molecular and cellular mechanisms that underlie the global orientation of mammalian hair follicles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Astn2 acts to bias the orientation of hair follicles in the anterior direction.
the Astn2 ex5 deletion acts as a recessively acting modifier of Fz6 -/ hair patterning in mice.
the Astn2 exon5 deletion causes a bias in the orientation of the hair follicles on the back of the Fz 6 -/- mouse, and this causes an orientation reversal in the hair follicles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Astrotactin is an endosome protein that regulates the global orientation of the hair follicle.
Astn2 is a genetic modifier that regulates the global orientation of mammalian hair follicles.
Astn2 is a modifier of PCP in the mouse hair follicle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Astn2 modulates the global orientation of the hair follicle array.
Astn2 modulates PCP and thus the orientation of mammalian hairs.
Astn2 is a genetic modifier of the PCP phenotype of Fz6 -/-.
